study: Gore et al. 2021, Quality Teaching Rounds (QTR) RCT, Teaching & Teacher Education
eval_evidence: Trial designed, conducted, and authored by the QTR developers (Gore et al., Univ. of Newcastle Teachers & Teaching Research Centre, who developed QT and QTR); not a third-party evaluation.
developer_evidence: Headline Researcher-led QTR arm (row 38): the 2-day workshop was delivered by the lead researcher who co-developed QT/QTR. (Trainer-led QTR arm, row 39, was delivered by trained QTR Advisers instead.)
cascade_evidence: Researcher-led QTR (primary arm) = developer trains teachers directly. The parallel Trainer-led QTR arm (row 39) IS a cascade: 3 QTR Advisers received 25 days of developer training then ran the workshops (train-the-trainer).
counterfactual_evidence: Extracted contrast is QTR (and QTR-T) vs the wait-list / PD-as-usual control. (The separate Peer Observation arm was an active-alternative control and was not the extracted comparison.)
coaching_evidence: After the 2-day workshop + 4 in-school PD days, teachers run Quality Teaching Rounds within their own school PLCs (peer observation/analysis); no ongoing external in-class coaching of individual teachers.
student_dose_evidence: Pedagogy-focused PD changing teachers' regular Stage-2 instruction; no student tutoring, pull-out, or added student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: Short PD delivered within one school year; single 8-month follow-up wave (Cohort 1); no multi-year rollout/maturity axis.
